traits.inflorescence.note: The Flora of North America's account of the family, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): inflorescences unisexual, the staminate catkins pendulous, elongate, cylindric and conspicuously bracteate; the pistillate erect to pendulous bracteate catkins, or compact clusters of two or three flowers under leafy involucres (the hazels).

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 61 Betulaceae (birches and alders) and 63 Corylaceae (hazels and hornbeams), which APG joins as Betulaceae: leaves alternate, simple, pinnately veined with prominent nerves, mostly toothed; stipules present, often falling early; flowers monoecious, the male in catkins; fruit a small nut, bare or winged in the birches and alders, held in a leafy husk in the hazels.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, family Betulaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, family Betulaceae: leaf margin serrate, toothed, usually; read as {"serrate": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, family Betulaceae: leaf habit deciduous; read as "deciduous".

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 335, family Betulaceae: inflorescence posture pendent (male catkins); read as "pendent". The books add erect (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 337, 338: pendent to erect.

traits.flowering_position.note: DELTA Betulaceae (read 2026-10-16): inflorescences terminal; male catkins at shoot tips or in lateral buds (Corylus), female on short shoots. 'both' is my reading.
